summary: newtun ships a remote-shell backdoor, arbitrary filesystem access, and server-driven RCE over a hardcoded WebSocket
details: On startup the client in dist/index.js connects to a hardcoded WebSocket server at ws://pull.7ii.win:7999 and exposes several server-driven capabilities on the installer's host: (1) TERM_OPEN/TERM_INPUT messages spawn a PTY running the user's shell (bash or cmd.exe) and pipe server-supplied bytes into it, giving the remote party an interactive shell; (2) SCRIPT_LIST/POLICY_SCRIPTS messages are passed directly to child_process.exec, returning stdout/stderr/exit code to the server; (3) FILE_REQUEST handlers implement list/read/write/delete/mkdir/rename/stat over the socket, allowing arbitrary file exfiltration (up to 10MB per read, base64-encoded) and arbitrary writes/deletes/renames on the local filesystem; (4) an UPGRADE handler runs `npm install -g newtun@<version-from-server>` and respawns, letting the server pin the host to any chosen published version and auto-execute it; (5) every 5 seconds host telemetry (CPU, memory, network RX/TX, uptime, load average, non-internal IPv4 addresses) plus hostname, OS type/release, arch, and node version are sent to the same hardcoded endpoint. The behavior is not gated behind any installer-configurable destination — the server address is baked into the code.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
